description: Nitpicker Follow-up Tasks - close out the remaining actionable findings from the adversarial nitpicker.md review: reconcile the nitpicker.md checklist with the current code, make POST /feeds strictly non-blocking, correct stale session wording in the README, stop clobbering the DEBUG localStorage key on every load, and normalize the repo to the no-space-before-colon TypeScript style via a one-time mechanical cleanup (NO new lint rule or dependency - see US-005 notes for why). userStories.title: Make POST /feeds strictly non-blocking
userStories.description: As a user adding a feed, I want the request to return immediately so the UI is never blocked waiting on a slow upstream fetch.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /feeds inserts the feed row, pulls the discovery alarm forward (preserving the existing RESOLVE_WINDOW_MS targetAt behavior), then returns 201 with the freshly-inserted bare feed row WITHOUT awaiting fetchFeed
The initial fetchFeed runs entirely in the background via ctx.waitUntil after the response is constructed
Add a test where fetchFeed is slow/stubbed and assert the handler still responds promptly with 201 (response time independent of upstream feed latency)
Remove the now-unused awaitFetchOrTimeout helper and POST_HYBRID_WAIT_MS constant from src/server/durable-objects/index.ts; test/dead-code.mjs passes
Existing 409 (duplicate), 400, and validation paths for POST /feeds are unchanged
Tests pass
npm run lint passes
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: PRD US-002 / FR-2,3,4. Symbols confirmed in src/server/durable-objects/index.ts: RESOLVE_WINDOW_MS (l184), POST_HYBRID_WAIT_MS (l185), awaitFetchOrTimeout (l2548), handler ~l1626-1644. Keep the alarm pull-forward; only drop the wait. Bare-row 201 is already the slow-path response today, so no client depends on fetched metadata in the body (see PRD Design Considerations).

userStories.title: Correct README session wording (signed session-id cookies)
userStories.description: As a developer reading the README, I want an accurate description of the session model so I understand what rotating SESSION_SECRET does.
acceptanceCriteria: First confirm the actual implementation: sessions live in KV behind a random session id carried in a SIGNED cookie (not an encrypted cookie)

Replace 'encrypted cookies' / 'cannot be decrypted' wording with 'signed session-id cookies' in all three locations: the overview list, the SESSION_SECRET table row, and the 'Rotate SESSION_SECRET' section
The rotation section explains that rotating SESSION_SECRET invalidates existing signed cookie values (signatures no longer verify), so users must sign in again
Doc-only change: no code is modified and the session implementation is untouched
Typecheck passes (sanity check)
userStories.notes: PRD US-003 / FR-5,6. README only. Verify the session model in the server auth code before editing so the new wording is accurate.

userStories.title: Stop stomping the DEBUG localStorage key on load
userStories.description: As a developer, I want my customized DEBUG value to survive a page reload instead of being overwritten or deleted.
acceptanceCriteria: In dev/staging, DEBUG is seeded to 'rsss,rsss:*' ONLY when no DEBUG value already exists in localStorage (presence check via localStorage.getItem('DEBUG'))
An existing user-set DEBUG value is never overwritten or deleted on load: remove the unconditional setItem and the unconditional removeItem at src/client/index.ts lines ~41 and ~43
npm run lint passes
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: set a custom DEBUG value then reload and confirm it persists; with no DEBUG value set, confirm the default is seeded in dev
userStories.notes: PRD US-004 / FR-7,8. Target src/client/index.ts l38-44 (dev/staging gate confirmed). Resolve the production branch per PRD Open Questions (current code does removeItem in prod) - prefer leaving DEBUG untouched when absent unless there is a reason to force-off.

userStories.title: Normalize type-annotation colon spacing repo-wide (one-time cleanup)
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the whole repo conformed to the no-space-before-colon type-annotation style so the codebase is consistent (entitled:boolean, not entitled: boolean).
acceptanceCriteria: Convert type-annotation colons to the house no-space style across all .ts/.js files: entitled:boolean, classes?:string[], (x:number):string, const a:number = x

Use an AST-aware transform, NOT a naive ': ' -> ':' regex - a regex would corrupt object literals ({ a: b }), ternaries (a ? b : c), switch case labels, and labeled statements. Target ONLY type-annotation colons: property/method signatures, variable and parameter annotations, function/method return types, index signatures, type aliases
Run the transform as a throwaway script (in scratch space) built on already-installed tooling (the TypeScript compiler API or @typescript-eslint/parser); do not commit the script
Do NOT add any eslint rule, plugin, or dependency, and do NOT modify .eslintrc - honors the project 'never change eslint settings' rule; package.json and the lockfile are unchanged
Arrow spacing (=>) and non-type colons (object literals, ternaries, case labels) are left untouched
The cleanup is mechanical only - the git diff contains only whitespace changes adjacent to type-annotation colons; no behavioral code changes
npm run lint passes (existing rules unchanged)
npm test passes
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: PRD US-005 + US-006, REVISED 2026-06-23 after research + user decision. The PRD's FR-9 (add @typescript-eslint/type-annotation-spacing) is NOT viable: that rule was REMOVED in the installed typescript-eslint plugin v8 (8.53.1 ships 0 formatting rules), and ESLint Stylistic (@stylistic/eslint-plugin) is not installed. User chose a one-time cleanup with NO enforcement rule and NO new dependency - the style may regress later without a guard, which is an accepted tradeoff. House style confirmed by user: no space on EITHER side of the type-annotation colon. SCALE: if many files violate, the AST codemod must handle them - do not hand-edit hundreds of files. Finding completeness has no lint-rule checker now, so spot-check with heuristic greps after the codemod.
